text.p: These are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers.
- The Slovenian parliament on Tuesday ratified the association agreement with the European Union by 70 votes to three after a prolonged debate.

- The European Commission said Slovenia should be in the first round of countries invited to start negotiations on full EU membership, along with the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Estonia and Cyprus.
- Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prlic met Slovenian officials on Tuesday and said the two countries should continue to improve economic cooperation.

- The Organisation of European Cooperation and Development (OECD) said Slovenia's key tasks in the future should be to reduce inflation, restructure the banking sector and pension systems and limit the growth of salaries.
- The city of Ljubljana adopted a budget for 1997 on Tuesday, whereby spending was expected to amount to 27 billion tolars ($165.4 million).
- The Constitutional Court said the monopoly of state-owned mobile telephone system operator Mobitel was unconstitutional.
- The public prosecution service is investigating whether the city of Ljubljana has paid an excessive price for coal imported from Indonesia in the past couple of years.
- The government and the state pension fund have not yet come to an agreement on the fund's 1997 financial plan.
- Henkel Austria became a sole owner of its Slovenian branch Henkel-Zlatorog after purchasing Zlatorog's 49 percent stake in the company for 14 million marks ($7,8 million).
- Most of the companies listed on the Ljubljana stock exchange expect their higher profits in 1997 than last year.
